You are a senior product/UI designer (think Linear, Zapier, Notion quality bar). Read-only: do not edit files.

Look at the current product: screenshots /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/design/*.png (look at every one), UI code in /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/web/src/ (App.tsx, components/Routines.tsx, DecisionCard.tsx, EvidenceDrawer.tsx, SourceAnchors.tsx, StatusStrip.tsx, ui/button.tsx, index.css for design tokens: ink/ink-2/ink-3, line, panel, ok blue #1d6fe0, stop red, level colors red/amber/grey/blue). Stack: React 19 + Tailwind v4 + lucide-react + radix dialog; no other UI libs installed (check web/package.json). Backend: src/ask_soony/routines.py (routines are Python code an LLM writes from building blocks open_cards/carry_out/notify/log/first_time/now, run in a sandbox; each has name, description in buyer language, code, enabled, runs[] with did[] steps and log).

Problem: routines are currently shown as a name, a sentence and raw Python in a side sheet. Buyers (procurement people, not developers) must be able to SEE, TRUST and CHANGE them. The team wants: visualise the routines, allow edits by writing ("also tell me on Teams", "only for Polish suppliers") or by drag and drop, and offer creating/changing routines also after a voice/phone conversation.

Design and specify, concretely enough to implement directly:
1. A visual representation of one routine that a buyer understands at a glance: e.g. "When … / And … / Then … / Unless it costs money → ask me" blocks (Zapier/Shortcuts-like), with live stats (handled N cards, last run, what it did). Propose the data shape the LLM should return next to the code so the UI can render it reliably (e.g. {trigger: [...conditions as plain phrases + machine fields], steps: [{kind: notify|carry_out|log, text, ...}], guard: ...}). Decide: should code be generated FROM this structure deterministically (so drag-drop edits are safe) or stay LLM-written with the structure as a description? Recommend one with reasons (safety, demo reliability, time).
2. Editing: natural-language edit box (what the request/response loop looks like, showing a diff of the blocks before applying, re-running the dry run), and drag-and-drop (which elements are draggable: reorder steps, drag a building block from a palette, remove a condition). Say what is worth building in the time (one dev, ~3 hours for this whole area) and what is a fake you should not build.
3. Where routines live in the UI: a dedicated view vs the side sheet, how a card that a routine handled looks in the inbox/activity, how the "automate this" offer looks after a decision (currently a bottom toast, see 7-automate-offer.png), and an offer after a voice conversation.
4. Concrete component list with Tailwind-level layout notes (sizes, colors from the existing tokens), and copy (exact button/label texts, no internal codes like amber/level/routine_type).
5. Quick wins to make the whole UI feel like one product (consistency issues you see in the screenshots).
Keep it under ~1000 words, prioritized.

content.text:
I looked at all 7 screenshots, `Routines.tsx`, `App.tsx`, `DecisionCard.tsx`, `Rail.tsx`, `StatusStrip.tsx`, `VoiceCall.tsx`, `button.tsx`, `index.css` and `routines.py`. Here is the plan, most important first.

## 1. The model: the LLM writes a spec, a compiler writes the code

**Recommendation:** the LLM returns only a structured spec. A small Python compiler (about 40 lines in `routines.py`) turns that spec into the same `soony` Python, which still runs in the Monty sandbox. "Show the code" stays; it now shows compiled code.

Why this and not "the structure describes the LLM's code":
- **Safety.** Drag-and-drop and text edits change data, never code. The "costs money comes to you" rule is added by the compiler, so it cannot be left out.
- **Demo reliability.** The sandbox can't reject a draft anymore, so the repair round goes away. Before/after is a plain JSON comparison.
- **Time.** A description-only structure would drift from the code after the first edit, and the screen would show something the routine doesn't do.

Spec shape (replaces `code` in the writer prompt's JSON; `name` and `description` stay):
```json
{"when":[{"id":"c1","field":"evidence|option_action|option_to|supplier_name|supplier_country|kind",
          "op":"contains|is|in","value":"ready for pick-up","text":"the papers say goods are ready for pick-up"}],
 "then":[{"id":"s1","do":"carry_out","match":{"to":"DC site lead","action_contains":"collect"},
          "text":"Send the collect message to the DC site lead"},
         {"id":"s2","do":"notify","channel":"phone|teams|both","text":"Tell me on Teams"},
         {"id":"s3","do":"log","text":"Note it in the history"}]}
```
- Conditions are combined with AND. Every card is handled once (the compiler always uses `first_time`).
- The "costs money" rule is not in the spec; it is always added.
- IDs must stay stable across edits; the prompt says "keep ids of unchanged items".

Two backend gaps:
- `notify()` always sends both phone and Teams. It needs a `channel` argument, otherwise "also tell me on Teams" changes nothing.
- "Only for Polish suppliers" needs `supplier_country` in `_card_view` (from master data). Without it, the editor must answer "I can't filter by country yet" rather than guess.

## 2. How one routine looks (`RoutineFlow`)

Card frame: `rounded-xl border border-line bg-white p-4`.
- **Header:** name (`text-[16px] font-bold`) and a real switch (`h-5 w-9 rounded-full`, `bg-ok` when on, `bg-line` when off). It replaces the On/Off pill, which looks like a button.
- **Stats line** (`text-sm text-ink-3`): "Handled 3 cards · Last ran 03:39 · Nothing to do". Add a `handled` counter on the backend, because `runs` keeps only the last 20.
- **Blocks:** stacked vertically, joined by a connector (`ml-6 h-3 w-px bg-line`). Each block is `rounded-lg border border-line px-3 py-2.5 text-[15px]` with a label column `w-14 text-xs font-bold uppercase tracking-wide`.
  - **When** (label `text-ink-3`): conditions as chips, `rounded-md bg-panel px-2 py-1 text-sm ring-1 ring-line`. Show the `text` phrase, never the field names.
  - **Then** (label `text-ok`): one row per step with a lucide icon:
    - `Send` for "carry out"
    - `Smartphone` / `MessageSquare` for "tell me" (phone / Teams)
    - `NotebookPen` for the log
  - **Always** (fixed, `border-dashed bg-panel`, `Lock` icon): "Costs money? It comes to you to decide." No delete button and not draggable.
- **Footer:** "Run now" and "Delete" (keep the current ones), then "Show the code", collapsed.

## 3. Editing (about 3 hours, in this order)

**Build (45 min): the change box.**
- Under the blocks: an input (`h-10 rounded-lg border-line`) with placeholder "Change it in your words, e.g. “also tell me on Teams”", plus a small button "Change".
- New endpoint `POST /api/routines/{id}/edit {instruction}`. The LLM gets the old spec and the allowed fields, returns a new spec; the server compiles it, does a dry run, and returns `{before, after, preview}`.
- The client compares blocks by ID:
  - Added: `bg-ok/5 ring-1 ring-ok/40` with a small "New" tag.
  - Removed: `opacity-60 line-through` with a "Removed" tag in `text-stop`.
  - Changed: the old phrase struck through, then the new one.
- Below that, "Test on today's inbox:" with the existing `Steps` component. Buttons: "Apply change" (disabled if the test failed) and "Keep as is".

**Build (30 min): direct manipulation, no library.**
- An × on hover removes a condition chip or a step (re-compile, then the same review step before saving).
- Native HTML5 drag-and-drop (`draggable`, `onDragOver`) reorders "Then" steps.
- A small palette under "Then" with three chips you can drag or click: "Tell me on my phone", "Tell me on Teams", "Note it in the history".

**Don't build:**
- A node-graph or canvas editor.
- Dragging new conditions in (they need value entry; use the change box).
- Picking a different carry-out target by dragging.
- Editable Python.
- Changing a routine live by voice during the call.

## 4. Where routines live and how they show up

- **Location:** keep the side sheet, widened to `sm:max-w-[560px]`. A separate page isn't worth it in 3 hours.
  - Rename the button "Routines" and always show the label.
  - Swap the `Cog` icon for `Workflow`; the cog reads as settings and its badge reads as a notification.
  - Remove the second "Routines" pill floating over the Europe map inset (screenshots 6 and 7).
- **Draft view:** same `RoutineFlow` in `border-2 border-ok/50 bg-ok/5`, with the test run between the blocks and the buttons "Turn on" / "Not now".
- **Cards a routine handled:** add a `via` field to activity items (the backend already passes `via: "routine: <name>"` to `approve`). Those rows get a chip: `Workflow` icon, `text-xs font-semibold text-ok bg-ok/10 rounded px-1.5`, "By routine · Tell DC site lead to collect at port". Clicking it opens the sheet scrolled to that routine.
- **Paid options a routine looked at:** the card stays in "Needs you" with a line above the buttons: "Your routine ‘…’ checked this. It costs money, so it's yours."
- **"Automate this" offer.** Right now there are two that disagree:
  - The bottom toast covers the map and legend.
  - `DecisionCard.tsx` lines 201–212 show a different, hard-coded "Send routine ETA chasers… Allow always / Ask me each time".

  Replace both with one panel pinned at the top of the right column (`rounded-xl border-2 border-ok/40 bg-ok/5 p-4`):
  - "Approved: Collect game card case from the port"
  - "Handle the next one like this on its own?"
  - "You'll see what it would do before it starts. Anything that costs money still comes to you."
  - Buttons: "Show me how" (writes the draft and opens the sheet) and "Not now".
- **After a voice call:**
  - When the call ends with a decision, the same panel appears inside the call area, headed "You decided this on the phone."
  - Add a realtime tool, `suggest_routine(instruction)`, for when the buyer says "do that automatically next time". The server drafts it, the assistant replies "I've drafted it. Check it on screen before it starts", and a push says "Routine draft ready to review".
  - Voice never turns a routine on.

## 5. Quick wins for consistency

1. One way of offering automation and one set of words for it (see section 4).
2. Cost wording: "none" (screenshot 1) and "No cost" (screenshot 7) both appear. Use "No cost" everywhere.
3. Section headings: "NEEDS YOU" is `text-sm font-bold`, the sheet headings are `text-xs font-semibold`. Pick one: `text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-ink-3`.
4. The list of decided cards shows the raw lowercase status ("approved"). Use the existing `DONE_WORD` map and give titles two lines (`line-clamp-2`) instead of cutting them off.
5. The floating "Enable alerts" pill covers the Activity list (screenshot 7). Move it into the header next to the bell.
6. Mobile (screenshot 5): the status strip runs off the screen and the header buttons wrap under it. On small screens, hide "Breaks first" and use `min-w-0`.
7. Collector's shows "−7 h slack" while "On track". Show "–" or "+7 h" instead; a negative number next to "On track" reads as a bug.
8. The notify title in `push.send` starts with an emoji ("⚙️ {name}"). Use "Routine: {name}" to match the plain, emoji-free UI.

### Time plan
| Task | Time |
|---|---|
| Spec, compiler, writer prompt changes, `notify` channel | 45 min |
| `RoutineFlow` and draft view | 45 min |
| Change box, before/after, test run | 45 min |
| Remove, reorder, palette | 30 min |
| "By routine" chips, one offer panel, voice offer | 15 min |

### Critical files
- /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/src/ask_soony/routines.py
- /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/web/src/components/Routines.tsx
- /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/web/src/App.tsx
- /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/web/src/components/DecisionCard.tsx
- /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/web/src/components/Rail.tsx
- /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony/web/src/components/VoiceCall.tsx
